source_text:
Ἐκδεχώμεθα οὖν καθ̓ ῶραν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ, ἐπειδὴ οὐκ οἴδαμεν τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς ἐπιφανείας τοῦ θεοῦ.
ἐπερωτηθεὶς γὰρ αὐτὸς ὁ κύριος ὑπό τινος, πότε ἥξει αὐτοῦ ἡ βασιλεία, εἶπεν: Ὅταν ἔσται τὰ δύο ἕν, καὶ τὸ ἔξω ὡς τὸ ἔσω, καὶ τὸ ἄρσεν μετὰ τῆς θηλείας οὔτε ἅρσεν οὔτε θῆλυ.
τὰ δύο δὲ ἕν ἐστιν, ὅταν λαλῶμεν ἑαυτοῖς ἀλήθειαν καὶ ἐν δυσὶ σώμασιν ἀνυποκρίτως εἴη μία ψυχή.
καὶ τὸ ἔξω ὡς τὸ ἔσω, τοῦτο λέγει: τὴν ψυχὴν λέγει τὸ ἕσω, τὸ δὲ ἔξω τὸ σῶμα λέγει. ὃν τρόπον οὖν σου τὸ σῶμα φαίνεται, οὕτως καὶ ἡ ψυχή σου δῆλος ἔστω ἐν τοῖς καλοῖς ἔργοις.
καὶ τὸ ἄρσεν μετὰ τῆς θηλείας, οὔτε ἄρσεν οὔτε θῆλυ, τοῦτο λέγει: ἵνα ἀδελφὸς ἰδὼν ἀδελφὴν οὐδὲν φρονῇ περὶ αὐτῆς θηλυκόν, μηδὲ φρονῇ τι περὶ αὐτοῦ ἀρσενικόν.
ταῦτα ὑμῶν ποιούντων, φησίν, ἐλεύσεται ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ πατρός μου.
thought_title: The Kingdom Comes When Two Become One
orientation: The preacher is urging the congregation to await God's kingdom hour by hour, and now explains the Lord's saying about when the kingdom will come.
pass_a_gloss: Let us await therefore hour by hour the kingdom of God in love and righteousness, since we do not know the day of the appearing of God. For having been asked himself the Lord by someone, when will come his kingdom, he said: When will be the two one, and the outside as the inside, and the male with the female neither male nor female. The two but one is, when we speak to ourselves truth and in two bodies without hypocrisy may be one soul. And the outside as the inside, this he says: the soul he says the inside, the outside but the body he says. In what manner therefore your body appears, so also your soul let it be clear in the good works. And the male with the female, neither male nor female, this he says: that a brother seeing a sister should think nothing about her female, nor should she think anything about him male. These things you doing, he says, will come the kingdom of my father.

choices.english: Let us await therefore hour by hour
choices.why: The verb means to await expectantly, not merely to wait; 'hour by hour' preserves the distributive sense of καθ' ὥραν.
rejected: Let us wait therefore every hour

choices.why: The glossary fixes ἐπιφάνεια as 'appearing'; the genitive is objective, the day when God appears.
The saying is deliberately terse and paradoxical; keeping the bare predicate 'one' without 'become' preserves the force of the Lord's words.

choices.english: we speak truth to one another
choices.why: ἑαυτοῖς is a reciprocal dative, 'to one another'; the phrase means truthful speech among believers.

choices.term: ἐν δυσὶ σώμασιν ἀνυποκρίτως εἴη μία ψυχή
choices.english: there is one soul in two bodies without hypocrisy
choices.why: The optative εἴη expresses a wish or possibility; 'without hypocrisy' modifies the unity of soul, not the bodies.
rejected: one soul may be in two bodies unhypocritically
in two bodies there would be one soul without pretense

choices.term: ἀδελφὸς ἰδὼν ἀδελφὴν οὐδὲν φρονῇ περὶ αὐτῆς θηλυκόν
choices.english: a brother who sees a sister should think nothing female about her
choices.why: φρονῇ is subjunctive with ἵνα, expressing purpose; 'think nothing female about her' keeps the adjective as predicate of the thought, not the person.
rejected: a brother seeing a sister should not think of her as female
a brother who sees a sister should have no female thought about her

pass_b_english: Since we do not know the day of God's appearing, let us await the kingdom of God hour by hour in love and righteousness.
For when the Lord himself was asked by someone when his kingdom would come, he said: "When the two will be one, and the outside as the inside, and the male with the female neither male nor female."
Now the two are one when we speak truth to one another, and in two bodies there may be one soul without hypocrisy.
And "the outside as the inside" means this: the inside is the soul, and the outside is the body. So just as your body is visible, let your soul be evident in good works.
And "the male with the female, neither male nor female" means this: that a brother who sees a sister should think nothing female about her, nor should he think anything male about himself.
When you do these things, the Lord says, the kingdom of my Father will come.

problems.quote: think nothing female about her, nor should she think anything male about him
problems.source_quote: ἵνα ἀδελφὸς ἰδὼν ἀδελφὴν οὐδὲν φρονῇ περὶ αὐτῆς θηλυκόν, μηδὲ φρονῇ τι περὶ αὐτοῦ ἀρσενικόν
problems.why: The Greek uses third person: 'a brother...should think...nor should [he] think' (both about the brother's thoughts). English adds 'she think' about him, changing agency and making the sister an active subject.
problems.fix: nor should he think anything male about himself

edits.old: nor should she think anything male about him
edits.new: nor should he think anything male about himself

fixed: The English 'nor should she think anything male about him' was corrected to 'nor should he think anything male about himself' to match the Greek third-person subject.

problems.quote: think nothing female about her, nor should he think anything male about himself
problems.source_quote: οὐδὲν φρονῇ περὶ αὐτῆς θηλυκόν, μηδὲ φρονῇ τι περὶ αὐτοῦ ἀρσενικόν
problems.why: English 'nor should he think anything male about himself' — Greek ἀρσενικόν is neuter adjective 'something male,' object of φρονῇ. 'About himself' is interpretive but captures the reflexive context. The sense is: he should not think of himself as male (in a sexual way) toward her. This is a reasonable literary rendering.

problems.quote: in two bodies there is one soul without hypocrisy
problems.source_quote: ἐν δυσὶ σώμασιν ἀνυποκρίτως εἴη μία ψυχή
problems.why: English 'there is' for εἴη (optative 'may be') loses the optative wish/possibility mood. Changes modality from 'may there be' to indicative statement.
problems.fix: and in two bodies there may be one soul without hypocrisy
problems.ruling: εἴη is optative ('may there be'); 'there is' makes indicative statement, losing optative mood.

edits.old: in two bodies there is one soul without hypocrisy
edits.new: in two bodies there may be one soul without hypocrisy

edits.old: nor should he think anything male about himself
edits.new: nor should he think anything male about her

fixed: The first problem was real: the optative mood was lost. Changed 'there is' to 'there may be'.
The second problem was real: the Greek object is 'about her,' not 'about himself.' Changed to 'about her.'

problems.quote: nor should he think anything male about her
problems.source_quote: μηδὲ φρονῇ τι περὶ αὐτοῦ ἀρσενικόν
problems.why: ἀὐτοῦ refers back to the brother (subject), not 'her'. Should be 'nor should he think anything male about himself'.
problems.fix: nor should he think anything male about himself
problems.ruling: αὐτοῦ is masculine referring to brother (ἀδελφὸς), not sister; 'about her' mistranslates the pronoun.

edits.old: nor should he think anything male about her
edits.new: nor should he think anything male about himself

problems.quote: When you do these things, he says, the kingdom of my Father will come
problems.why: Unclear whether 'he says' refers to Jesus or the author; the shift is abrupt after the author's interpretation.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'Jesus says' or 'the Lord says' to maintain the chain of attribution.

edits.old: When you do these things, he says, the kingdom of my Father will come.
edits.new: When you do these things, the Lord says, the kingdom of my Father will come.

fixed: The speaker attribution problem is real: the abrupt 'he says' after the author's interpretation is unclear. Changed to 'the Lord says' to maintain the chain of attribution.

last_rejected.why: English 'he said' after identifying 'the Lord himself' is clear. But the quotation marks and attribution are slightly ambiguous about whether 'he said' refers to the Lord or someone else. Actually clear enough.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter admits it is clear enough; εἶπεν after αὐτὸς ὁ κύριος is unambiguous.

last_rejected.why: 'εἴη' is optative, expressing a wish or potential. 'There may be' captures this. Correct.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter confirms 'there may be' correctly renders optative εἴη; no error.

last_rejected.why: 'δῆλος ἔστω' = 'let it be clear/evident'. 'Evident' is fine.
last_rejected.ruling: Reporter confirms 'evident' is fine for δῆλος ἔστω; no error.

last_rejected.quote: think nothing female about her, nor should he think anything male about himself
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐδὲν φρονῇ περὶ αὐτῆς θηλυκόν, μηδὲ φρονῇ τι περὶ αὐτοῦ ἀρσενικόν
last_rejected.why: The Greek says 'let him think nothing female about her, nor let him think anything male about himself.' The English 'should think' for φρονῇ (present subjunctive) changes modality from command to suggestion. Also 'nor should he' loses the μηδέ construction's force as a negative command.
last_rejected.fix: let him think nothing female about her, and let him not think anything male about himself
last_rejected.ruling: 'Should think' can render subjunctive φρονῇ in hina clauses; normal English range, not a major error.
